column4: Half the sky glowed gold, meeting the dark at the horizon like a sunrise; the sun is made only on the fourth day (1:14-19). Now white light from no source.
Radiant shafts of light poured through a widening gap, like sunlight through cloud; the sun is made only on the fourth day (1:14-19).
Set at dawn with golden light breaking over the land, before the sun is made (1:14-19), and the new land streaming wet; the text calls it dry land (1:9).
Set in midday sunshine before the sun is made (1:14-19), with young trees; the fruit trees already yield fruit (1:11-12).
Flocks of birds filled the sky; the text gives birds no number (1:20-22): now a few of each kind, while the waters teem (1:20-21).
Animals filled the plain like herds; the text gives no numbers (1:24-25): now a few of each kind, scattered.
Animals and birds 'gather' at a distance, a crowd the text doesn't number; now only a few, no herds (1:24-25).
Called the land a vast garden before Eden is planted (2:8), and had everything glowing; now a green land with a few animals.
Showed herds sleeping in the meadows; the text gives no herds (1:24-25, 2:1): now a few animals.
The tree of life glowed softly, a sign the text doesn't give (2:9); and streams became the one river that waters the garden (2:10).
Showed gold nuggets and gemstones glinting on a riverbank; the text only says the land of Havilah has gold, bdellium and onyx (2:11-12).
The fruit was 'gleaming', a sign the text doesn't give (2:17, 3:6); now plain ripe fruit.
Animals filed past in pairs, 'every creature has its mate'; the text says neither (2:19-20): now a few of each kind.
The fruit was 'gleaming' and the serpent 'beautiful', on a branch; the text gives none of these (3:1-6).
Mixed the hiding with Adam blaming Eve, and had the serpent slipping away, which the text doesn't say; now the hiding of 3:8-10.
Showed the ground turning to thorns and thistles at the garden's edge; the thorns are a curse to come (3:17-18), not seen happening.
Set at an 'eastern gate'; the text has no gate, only Cherubim and a flaming sword at the east of the garden (3:24).
Added a hut of branches and stone the text doesn't have (4:1-2); now no dwelling, and only the four it names.
Showed two stone altars, Abel's smoke rising straight and Cain's drifting low; the text gives no altar, fire or such sign (4:3-5).
Had Abel talking and Cain silent; the text says Cain talked with Abel (4:8).
Showed the mark as a faint glow on Cain's brow; the text doesn't say what or where the mark was (4:15).
Showed newborn Seth with a household calling on the LORD at an altar; that calling began in Enos's day (4:26), and the text has no altar.
Used Adam's young cast key at the end of his nine hundred and thirty years (5:5); now described in words as a very old man, with no key.
Dropped a caravan of families with donkeys travelling along a river; the text has no journey here (5:6-20).
Called Enoch old at three hundred and sixty-five, young beside the others' spans (5:20, 5:27), and added family watching; the text has no witnesses (5:24).
Dropped oxen and ploughs the text doesn't have, and kept to the six men it names (5:25-32).
Had giant warriors carrying spears; the text gives them no weapons, and doesn't say who the sons of God were (6:2-4).
Showed a house in flames, an event the text doesn't have (6:5-7).
Showed smoke rising over a corrupt city the text doesn't have, and Noah's wife without the sons' wives; now Noah and the three sons the text names (6:9-10).
Called the trees cypress-like, settling what gopher wood was, and put a storm on the horizon; the text gives neither (6:14).
Called the ark a ship with a hull, and had the family building and loading it; the text has Noah do all that God commanded (6:22).
Called the ark a ship, and added a ramp and pairs of animals; the text has a door in the side (6:16) and clean beasts by sevens (7:2).
Had long lines of animals going up a ramp, and no sons' wives in the cast; the text has a side door (6:16) and eight going in (7:7).
Showed animals on a ramp and the family at the door without the sons' wives; now the shut door as the flood begins, the ark not yet afloat (7:16-17).
Showed mountain peaks still above the water; all the high hills and the mountains were covered (7:19-20).
Called the ark a ship; it is the box of 6:14-16.
Had peaks emerging as the ark landed, seen from a neighbouring slope; the tops were seen only later (8:4-5), bare, with water all around.
Called the ark a ship and framed Noah from below, high up; now seen from far off, with water still on the face of the whole earth (8:9).
Showed green hillsides and the family crowding the window; the waters had only abated, the ground dry later (8:11, 8:13-14), and the dove came to Noah.
Showed Noah's wife and sons beside him over green land; Noah alone removed the covering and looked (8:13), and the text says dry, not green.
Showed the animals pouring out ahead of the family, down a ramp onto green slopes; Noah's family went forth first, the sons' wives with them (8:18-19).
Left out the sons' wives; all eight came out of the ark together (8:18).
Showed herds of wild beasts, though few of each kind left the ark (7:2-3, 8:19); now Noah and his sons, whom God blessed (9:1), without the wives.
Showed Noah's wife but not the sons' wives, amid many animals; God spoke to Noah and his sons (9:8), and few of each kind left the ark (7:2-3).
Had the sons and their families harvesting and treading grapes in a winepress; the text has Noah plant the vineyard (9:20), and no one else at work.
Added Ham's young son Canaan; the text doesn't put Canaan there or give his age (9:25).
Had Noah's sons watching their descendants load boats and sail away; the text has the isles divided among Japheth's sons, and no voyage (10:2-5).
Gave Nimrod hounds and a leopard skin, and the new cities' towers; the text gives none of these, and the tower comes later (11:4).
Showed the earth seeming to part; readers differ on 'the earth was divided' (10:25), so only the clans part, as the nations were divided (10:32).
Had the builders pause and look up at the light; the text doesn't say they saw the LORD come down (11:5).
Showed the tower's top broken; the text says only that they left off building (11:8).
Showed the brick towers of Ur; the text gives Ur no tower (11:28, 11:31).
Added a temple tower and children in the lane, and mourned Haran beside the married couples; the marriages may have come later (11:28-29), and Sarai had no child (11:30).
Had Ur's temple tower behind them; the text gives none (11:31).
